message.reasoning:
I need to decide on an auction bid for North Carolina Avenue.

I have $726 and a pink monopoly with four houses on each property. The opponent has $29 and a Boardwalk monopoly with four houses. I am considering whether to bid aggressively or conservatively.

p3 is bankrupt. p4 has $763 and a light blue monopoly. The auction is at $71 with p2 and p4 as the only bidders. I will bid up to about $150 and then drop.

If I win the auction, I can mortgage North Carolina Avenue back for $150 and net cash. This also blocks p4 from completing a green monopoly with Pennsylvania Avenue. Pacific Avenue is mortgaged by p1, so p4 cannot finish that set without trading.

Winning North Carolina Avenue would net $78 cash after paying the bid. It would also block p4 from completing a green monopoly. p1 might trade Pacific Avenue to survive, but that dark blue set is still dangerous.

The pink monopoly yields $625, $750, and $800 in rent with four houses. The light blue set is weaker at roughly $160 per property.

The dark blue set is the real danger. Park Place with three houses pays $1100 and Boardwalk with four pays $1700. If p1 lands on my pink monopoly with only $29 cash, they could go bankrupt and give me their entire set. I am currently on Pennsylvania Avenue, which belongs to p4 and is mortgaged.

I will bid the minimum $72 raise. p4 has $763 and can afford any rent. I will keep raising by one dollar to push p4 past my $150 cap. If they drop before that, I win North Carolina Avenue for a profit.

I will bid the minimum $72 raise rather than jumping ahead. I am checking whether mortgaging North Carolina Avenue can happen immediately.

Mortgaging is allowed in standard Monopoly. If I win the auction but cannot mortgage immediately, I will be down $72 cash. I can still afford this because my pink monopoly generates rent. However, landing on Boardwalk or Park Place would leave a shortfall of over $900. I can sell my pink houses for half their cost to cover that gap.

Selling all twelve pink houses and mortgaging the three properties would raise only about $1546. That is still $154 short of the $1700 Boardwalk rent. The dark blue threat remains severe.

I can survive a Park Place hit by selling houses, but Boardwalk is fatal even with all assets liquidated. Buying North Carolina Avenue for $72 or $150 would not improve my maximum liquidity, because mortgaging it back would recover the same cash. The property does not raise my survival ceiling.

Winning North Carolina Avenue for $72 would raise my maximum liquidity to about $1624, which is still below the $1700 Boardwalk rent. The extra cash does not change the fatal outcome. Blocking p4 from a second green is limited because Pacific Avenue belongs to p1, who may trade it for cash.

The bank has no houses left. Twelve hotels remain, but none are built yet. Building a green monopoly is impossible without selling houses back to the bank.

p4 has been matching every bid from $30 to $71. They are committed and may push the auction past my $150 cap. Blocking the green monopoly is mainly a long-term denial strategy, since no houses remain in the bank to build on immediately.

message.reasoning:
I need to decide on an auction bid for North Carolina Avenue.

I have $726 and a near-monopoly on the pink set. The only opponent with cash is p1, who has $29 and a strong Boardwalk/Atlantic/Short Line setup. p3 is bankrupt.

p4 has $763 and a light blue monopoly. The auction is at $75 with p2 and p4 as the only bidders. I will bid up to about $150, mortgage North Carolina Avenue, and block p4 from completing the PA+NC pair.

p4 already owns the mortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue. Completing the green set would require trading with p1, who holds Pacific. No houses remain in the bank, so building is impossible. The $150 cap reflects North Carolina's mortgage value.

Boardwalk with four houses charges $1700 and Park Place with three charges $1100. I am currently on Pennsylvania Avenue, so landing there would be expensive. After bidding for North Carolina, I would have roughly $576 to $650 left.

Selling all twelve pink houses would yield $600. Mortgaging St. Charles, States, and Virginia would add roughly $220 more. Combined with the cash left after bidding for North Carolina, this should cover the $1700 Boardwalk rent.

Liquidating all houses and mortgaging the pinks still leaves a gap of about $524 against the $1700 Boardwalk rent. The difference between buying North Carolina or not is negligible compared to that $1700 danger. Park Place with three houses charges $1100, which I can cover with my current cash plus house sales.

Bidding up to $150 leaves me with about $1176, which is tight but still covers the $1100 Park Place rent. The main strategic concern is that p4 could trade with p1 for the green monopoly if they win North Carolina. I would recover the cash by mortgaging immediately.

Mortgaging immediately after winning the auction is standard Monopoly. At $76 I would net $74 cash and deny p4 the property. Even at $149 I would gain $1 cash plus block them. p4 has matched every bid so far and may push to $150.

I will keep bidding. Each raise costs nothing if I drop later, and it forces p4 to pay more. The $76 bid is safe even if p4 drops out. I am checking whether p4's light blue monopoly with four houses changes the $150 cap.
